nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be measurable real random variables on a probability space. If $X$ and $Y$ are independent and $X + Y$ has a Gaussian law, then $X$ and $Y$ each have a Gaussian law. Here a Gaussian law may be degenerate, that is, a point mass.

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $(\mu_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of probability measures on the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $\varphi : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{C}$. Suppose that for every $t \in \mathbb{R}^d$ the characteristic functions $\hat\mu_n$ of the $\mu_n$ satisfy $\hat\mu_n(t) \to \varphi(t)$ as $n \to \infty$, and that $\varphi$ is continuous at $0$.
